title: Spark Catalyst Optimizer & Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)
exp: Deep-dive into Spark query planning: Unresolved Logical Plan → Analyzed → Optimized → Physical Plan, and AQE runtime optimizations.
pts: **Catalyst Optimizer pipeline:** rule-based transformations, constant folding, predicate pushdown, projection pruning.
**AQE (Adaptive Query Execution):** dynamic coalescing of shuffle partitions, dynamic join strategy switching (SortMerge to Broadcast), dynamic skew join handling.
**Skew Join Optimization:** splitting skewed partitions into sub-partitions and duplicating broadcast side rows.
**Dynamic Partition Pruning (DPP):** filtering partition directories at runtime using dimension table join predicates.

# Automatically detects and splits skewed partitions during Shuffle

Configure and verify AQE skew join handling on a skewed dataset

r: Deep mechanics of Spark Catalyst Optimizer & Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) under concurrent execution.
Always design for idempotency, cancellation propagation, and thread safety.
Memory allocation spikes or CPU bound thread starvation.

Balancing developer velocity with operational maintenance complexity.

qa.q: How does Spark AQE dynamically convert a SortMergeJoin to a BroadcastHashJoin at runtime?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** During initial shuffle stage execution, AQE measures actual materialized output partition sizes. If one side of the join is smaller than spark.sql.adaptive.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold, Spark dynamically changes the physical execution plan from SortMergeJoin to BroadcastHashJoin without re-running the query.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** SQL Server query processor constructs a logical tree, estimates cardinality using statistics, and selects physical operators (Nested Loops, Hash Join, or Merge Join) based on cost and sorted indexes.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Cartesian products or missing join predicates can cause exponential disk tempdb spilling, memory grant exhaustion, and query timeouts under concurrent load.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Nested loops excel for indexed small lookups; Hash joins handle large unsorted sets at the cost of higher tempdb and memory grant usage.

qa.q: What causes data skew in PySpark joins and how does AQE mitigate it?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Data skew happens when a specific join key (e.g., NULL or default ID) has millions of rows assigned to a single executor partition. AQE detects partition size imbalance, splits the heavy skewed partition into smaller sub-partitions, and replicates matching keys from the join target.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** SQL Server query processor constructs a logical tree, estimates cardinality using statistics, and selects physical operators (Nested Loops, Hash Join, or Merge Join) based on cost and sorted indexes.
